tasks.prompt: DO readings in the aeration tank disagree between the morning and afternoon operators.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Morning readings with meter A average 1.2 mg/L lower than afternoon readings with meter B at the same points.
Meter A calibration check in saturated water reads 88 percent against 100 percent for meter B.
Meter A membrane is older and was last changed six months ago.
Process performance and effluent quality are steady through the day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Meter A with its aged membrane and failed calibration check is reading low, not a real daily DO swing
The tank DO truly falls every morning and recovers every afternoon
Meter B reads high because it is newer
The operators sample at different depths by habit

inference.explanation: A true daily swing would show in process performance, which is steady, and meter B passes its calibration check while meter A fails its own. Depth habit is not supported when the same points are specified. The failed check on meter A supports instrument error.

Primary blanket log
Meter calibration check record for both meters

clueText.nc-a: Flow summaries do not test meter accuracy.
clueText.nc-b: Primary blanket records cover a different unit.
clueText.nc-c: After a membrane change and calibration, meter A matched meter B within 0.2 mg/L.

tasks.prompt: Effluent ammonia results are reported high, but a parallel check at another lab reads much lower.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The plant lab ammonia samples were preserved and held 10 days before analysis, past the method hold time.
The outside lab analyzed its splits within 2 days and read 2 mg/L against the plant lab 9 mg/L.
Plant process records show stable nitrification and low effluent ammonia on the online trend.
Quality control standards run with the plant batch read correctly.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The outside lab method is wrong and the plant results are correct
The over held samples changed during storage, so the plant lab results do not represent the effluent at sampling
Nitrification truly failed for exactly the sampled days
The online trend analyzer is broken and hides high ammonia

inference.explanation: Standards read correctly, so the method itself worked, and stable process records with a low online trend argue against a real failure on only the sampled days. The hold time breach plus the fresh split result supports sample storage change.

Screenings log
Blower log

clueText.nc-b: Screenings records cover headworks.
clueText.nc-c: Blower records do not test sample storage.

evidence.label: One shift uses a 1 L cylinder and the other a 2 L cylinder with a different diameter, giving different settled volumes for the same sludge.
A side by side test of one sample in both cylinders differed by 90 mL/L at 30 minutes.
Stirring practice also differs, with one shift stirring the cylinder and the other not.
SVI calculated from the two shifts swings by 40 mL/g on the same sludge.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The sludge settleability truly changes completely between shifts
One shift is falsifying its results
Inconsistent settleometer equipment and technique between shifts is producing the conflicting results, not real sludge changes
The mixed liquor is replaced entirely each shift

inference.explanation: A side by side test on one sample reproducing the difference rules out real sludge change, replacement, and falsification as the explanation. Different cylinder sizes and stirring directly account for the swing.

Influent pH log

evidence.label: The flow display jumped from 200 L/s to 340 L/s in one minute and stayed exactly there.
Wet well levels, pump run hours, and downstream tank levels show no change matching a real surge.
The magnetic flow meter grounding ring is found corroded and its signal cable shield damaged.
A portable clamp on meter on the same line reads 205 L/s.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A real surge entered the plant without raising any levels
Both duty pumps sped up without any control change
The clamp on meter is wrong and the surge is real
Electrical noise from the damaged meter grounding and shielding is producing a false flow reading

inference.explanation: A real surge would move levels and pump records, which are unchanged, and pumps cannot speed up without a control change. The portable meter agreeing with normal operations plus the damaged grounding supports a false reading.

Digester log
Flow meter inspection record and the portable meter comparison

tasks.prompt: A hydrogen sulfide alarm sounds at a wet well where a worker was about to enter, and readings differ by height.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The gas detector reads 18 ppm hydrogen sulfide at the bottom of the wet well and 2 ppm at the rim.
The well receives septic force main discharge and has not been ventilated yet today.
A second calibrated detector confirms the bottom reading within 1 ppm.
The worker stayed out and no symptoms were reported.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Hydrogen sulfide, heavier than air, has pooled at the bottom of the unventilated wet well at a dangerous level
The detector is faulty and the well is safe to enter
Oxygen enrichment at the bottom is causing the alarm
The gas is methane rising from the bottom and pushing readings up at the rim

inference.explanation: A second calibrated detector confirms the reading, contradicting a faulty detector. Hydrogen sulfide alarms are not oxygen enrichment, and methane rises rather than pooling low. Septic discharge, no ventilation, and a high bottom with low rim reading fit pooled hydrogen sulfide.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Calibrated detector log by depth and the force main discharge record for the well
Effluent chlorine log
Influent flow summary

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-b: Chlorine records do not test wet well gas.
clueText.nc-c: Flow summaries do not measure gas by depth.

evidence.label: The air control valve position cycles fully open to fully closed in step with the DO swings.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

The blower surges mechanically and cannot hold pressure
The slow fouled probe feeds delayed readings to the controller, which overcorrects the air valve and makes DO appear to hunt
The control valve is oversized and is the only problem
